chunks: And Ishaq ibn Yazid asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): About a man who enters Mecca and cuts from its trees, so he said:
"Cut what encroaches upon you, and do not cut what has not entered upon your dwelling."

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.دَاخِلاً عَلَيْكَ: Encroaching upon you, entering your space
key_terms.شَجَرِهَا: Its trees, referring to the trees of Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on cutting trees in Mecca according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal nuance of preserving Mecca's sanctity by permitting the cutting of trees that encroach upon a person's private dwelling or space, while prohibiting the cutting of those outside one's domain. This ruling highlights the balance between practical necessity for residents and the broader reverence for the holy city's natural environment. It underscores the principle that the sanctity of Mecca is not absolute in a way that overrides individual property rights, but rather protects the general public and sacred spaces.
